candidate_relations.reason: Although fibrous dysplasia was the working diagnosis on biopsy and the patient had a prior excision labeled as fibrous dysplasia, the reference diagnosis is cavernous hemangioma. The CT ground-glass appearance and biopsy findings were interpreted as fibrous dysplasia, but the final/most likely diagnosis per the benchmark is cavernous hemangioma—a benign vascular lesion of bone that can mimic fibrous dysplasia radiologically and histologically. Fibrous dysplasia and cavernous hemangioma are distinct entities (fibro-osseous vs. vascular), making this a conflicting subtype rather than a partial component or equivalent.
